commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

# NightJar's bug tracker

A small local tracker that stands in for Jira in the course. Issues have keys
like `NJ-12`, a summary, a description, a status and comments.

```bash
make tracker                       # start it (fresh seed issues, new tokens)
cat ~/.nightjar-tracker/tokens.json
export NJ_TRACKER_TOKEN=<read or write token>
python3 tools/tracker/tracker.py search import csv
python3 tools/tracker/tracker.py get NJ-12
```

- **Two tokens.** The read token can search and read. Only the write token can
  create issues or add comments (the server answers 403 otherwise).
- **Search** returns issues whose summary or description contain every word
  you give (a word matches the start of a word, so `import` finds `imported`).
- **Data** lives in `~/.nightjar-tracker/`, outside the repository.

# [Diary] Bedtime in the skipped spring-forward hour saved as 03:30 with no warning, Slept shows 5h 30m

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the NightJar diary and set the time zone to America/Toronto.
2. Log a night with bedtime 2026-03-08 02:30 and wake time 2026-03-08 09:00 (the clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00 that night, so 02:30 does not exist).
3. Save, then look at the saved night.

## Expected

Not specified (see Notes). The user should at least be told that 02:30 doesn't exist on that date, rather than have the entry silently changed.

## Actual

- The night is saved with bedtime 03:30 (EDT). No warning or error is shown.
- Slept shows 5h 30m. The user typed 02:30 to 09:00, which reads as 6h 30m.

## Evidence

Reproduced through the same function the form uses (`local_input_to_aware`), then the UTC round trip the diary stores:

```
local_input_to_aware('2026-03-08T02:30', 'America/Toronto') -> 2026-03-08 02:30:00-05:00
stored as UTC:   2026-03-08 07:30:00+00:00
read back local: 2026-03-08 03:30:00-04:00
Night(bedtime, wake 09:00-04:00).duration = 5:30:00
```

Cause: `diary.py:153` does `datetime.fromisoformat(text).replace(tzinfo=zone(timezone))`, which attaches the zone to a wall time that doesn't exist and never validates it.

## Environment

main @ 5d87a7a, Python 3.12, America/Toronto, test data only.

## Notes

- Question for product: what should happen when a user enters a time in the skipped hour? Options: reject with a message, or accept and tell the user it was moved to 03:30. No requirement or story covers it (docs/ only has the "correct across DST" NFR, T-114-6).
- Related: NJ-11 (Done), the autumn clock change made Slept an hour off. That was a duration-subtraction bug, fixed in `Night.duration`. This one is on input, in the spring gap, and is not a regression of NJ-11.

Reproduced 1 of 1 times (code path); not yet checked in the browser. Related: NJ-11.
EOF

content.text:
I reproduced the bug and drafted a ticket. Nothing is filed yet.

**Reproduction.** I ran the same function the form uses, `local_input_to_aware` in `diary.py:153`. It attaches the zone to 02:30 on 2026-03-08 without checking that the time exists. The diary stores that as 07:30 UTC, which reads back as 03:30 EDT. Slept comes out as 5h 30m instead of 6h 30m. I did this at code level, not in the browser, and the draft says so.

**Searches.** I ran nine searches: DST, spring forward, bedtime, slept, clocks, clock change, time zone, log night and one more. Only two issues came close:
- **NJ-11** (Done): the autumn clock change made Slept an hour off. That was a duration-subtraction bug, fixed in `Night.duration`. This bug is on input in the spring gap, so it is related but different. It is not a regression, and the draft names NJ-11.
- **NJ-4** (Done): reminder skipped during quiet hours. It's unrelated.

No open ticket covers this bug, so the draft is a new ticket.

**Expected result.** No requirement or story covers a time entered in the skipped hour. The draft says "Not specified" and adds a note asking product whether to reject the entry or accept it with a warning.

The draft is at `bug-drafts/dst-spring-gap-bedtime.md`. Its summary is "[Diary] Bedtime in the skipped spring-forward hour saved as 03:30 with no warning, Slept shows 5h 30m".

**File this?**
